# Pooled observational analysis

## Scope and correction of the individual audits

This is a read-only comparison of one Selection attempt per condition. The original public SuperJSON requirements are now available. They explicitly require the option modes, distinct processing orders, filtering, causes, container round trips, named exports, inspection of existing Error handling, a new branch and a commit. The substantial feature implementations and branch/commit work therefore cannot be dismissed as unnecessary merely because the individual audits initially lacked the task wording. Formatting churn and retries are separable extra work.

The K1 and K2 audits’ statements that no B0 was available apply to their original isolated evidence, not this pooled record. Also, the K2 audit’s original formally-unsolved conclusion needs the recovery addendum: its initial grade remains recorded, but the first complete valid same-patch diagnostic passed. Sources below use `outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/` as the root; event numbers refer to `main_agent` events in each run’s `infer_logs/superjson-error-stack-serialization/turn_1/trajs.json` and the corresponding `audit/posthoc_selection_matched_superjson-error-stack-serialization_{B0,K0,K1,K2}.md`.

## Outcomes and execution

| Condition | Independent official evaluation | Local execution and retained functionality |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | F2P 80/80; P2P 116/116; reward 1 | A pre-change frames probe failed and later passed. A full local run failed the performance threshold under `--no-opt`; the filtered functional run passed. After restoring a cause guard, the final build and focused probe passed, but the full functional suite was not rerun on that final version (events 19–22, 49–52, 65–74). |
| K0 | F2P 79/80; P2P 116/116; reward 0 | Substantial partial correctness and all measured P2P retained. The failure was sanitization of a cause excluded by `classFilter`; the patch propagates the parent’s sanitization flag, consistent with the failure and contrary to the public filter requirement. Local redaction and annotation checks found issues that were revised; final local tests excluded the performance test (events 47–64). |
| K1 | F2P 80/80; P2P 116/116; reward 1 | An off-mode reproduction failed before editing; focused checks and a final filtered suite passed. The initial full local suite failed its timing threshold; a second reported timing figure is only a student claim behind truncated output (events 13–15, 21–24, 27–29, 42–45). |
| K2 | Original: reward 0, F2P 0/80, P2P 80/116 with missing report data. Same-patch diagnostic: F2P 80/80, P2P 116/116, reward 1. | Local frames, configuration, cause and nested-Map probes passed; two full local runs failed the timing threshold and a filtered run passed (events 41–44, 56–58, 62–69). |

Official results are in each `runs/capability_v1_matched_prompt_selection_superjson-error-stack-serialization_{B0,K0,K1}_r1/eval_output/superjson-error-stack-serialization/eval_result.json`; K2’s complete result is `runs/capability_eval_diagnostic_selection_K2_02/eval_output/superjson-error-stack-serialization/eval_result.json`. These are independent verifier results, not the students’ inline tests. P2P measures retained behavior on the verifier’s cases, not all legacy functionality; full success likewise means success on the evaluated cases.

K2’s original verifier recorded missing F2P entries and a missing `/logs/verifier/new-ctrf.json`; 0/80 does **not** show that 80 feature assertions ran and failed. Diagnostic invocation 01 did not run the evaluator. Invocation 02 evaluated the identical 13,143-byte saved patch once, without a student retry, code or test change, or changed evaluation environment. Its complete passing report is the recovered outcome under the saved policy, not evidence of an improved patch. The original report’s root failure remains unknown; neither Node/JIT nor the library is established as its cause. See `runs/evaluation_diagnostic_02_state.json` and the supplied evaluation-recovery addendum.

All four students ended normally and committed. B0 and K2 each had an intermediate visible segfault; subsequent builds succeeded. Local timing failures have no comparable measured baseline, so they do not establish patch-induced regressions. K1’s raw stack-frame text retained a URL and email in one local display, but the public requirement specifically describes sanitizing messages, so that observation alone is not a demonstrated violation.

## Costs and unnecessary work

| Condition | Returned/requested tools | Model requests | Input tokens, including cached subset | Output tokens | Wall seconds | SDK estimate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B0 | 37/37 | 21 | 1,179,143; cached 297,216 | 6,101 | 1,203.024 | $6.048 |
| K0 | 33/33 | 16 | 1,049,250; cached 357,248 | 7,269 | 1,000.892 | ~$5.428 |
| K1 | 22/22 | 10 | 634,253; cached 201,600 | 5,835 | 829.154 | ~$3.317 |
| K2 | 34/34 | 15 | 769,918; cached 173,696 | 6,208 | 914.896 initial; 1,476.782 recovered end-to-end | $4.005 |

Cached input is **part of**, not additional to, input tokens. Dollar figures are SDK proxy estimates, not settled CLI billing. K2’s recovered wall time includes triage and the 89.220-second actual diagnostic; it must not be added again or attributed entirely to student execution. Model/tool counts did not change during recovery.

All patches contain some unrelated formatting in `src/index.ts`. B0 also retried a nonexistent formatting path and temporarily flipped a guard (events 53–60, 65–71); K0 and K2 reran full suites after timing failures; K1 investigated performance without a measured baseline. These consumed resources, although investigation was not necessarily unreasonable. No run committed a new persistent test file; inline probes provide narrower, less repeatable coverage. K1 happened to use the fewest requests, tokens and initial wall time here, but one attempt cannot establish an efficiency effect.

## Input, observed behavior and attribution

B0 had no library. K0, K1 and K2 each had their respective text in both the actual prompt and first bridge request; their loaded files are at the corresponding `runs/capability_v1_matched_prompt_selection_superjson-error-stack-serialization_{K0,K1,K2}_r1/infer_logs/superjson-error-stack-serialization/turn_1/loaded_capabilities.md`. This establishes input entry, not use or causation.

K1’s pre-edit reproduction and boundary round trip (events 13–15, 27–29) are consistent with its reproduction and boundary-tracing guidance. K2’s serialize/parse and nested-Map probes (events 42–44, 62–65) are consistent with inspecting state across representation boundaries. K0’s circular-cause check (events 50, 52–60) is consistent with cycle-aware guidance. But B0 also inspected the existing implementation and built a failing frames reproduction before editing (events 1–12, 19–22). Such behavior is not distinctive proof of library adoption. K0’s filter failure has concrete patch-level support, but no evidence shows its library caused that implementation choice; K0’s guidance also called for observable contract checks. Conversely, its local checks missed the interaction. Similar caution applies to the passing runs.

K2 is not merely a different heading structure: its representation rule explicitly says a safety comparison must use meaningful units rather than physical layout and must not disable safety for unrelated categories. K1 separately calls for semantic preservation, equivalence or safety validation, and varied inputs, but does not state that specific constraint. K2 therefore supplies a substantive, transferable **qualification**, though whether it changes behavior on this serializer task is unshown. K2 also separates identity/failure feedback and persistent input contracts; K1 covers related concerns more compactly. The delivered texts differ in length and content—K1 578 words, K2 526—despite shared development sources and budgets, so this is not a controlled wording-only comparison. No source ablation supports ranking individual trajectories by marginal learning value. Shared harness preparation and guidance available even to B0 may also reduce observable differences, but that ceiling explanation is unverified.

## Selection disposition and closing assessment

Apply the saved rule: drop only for leakage, absent injection, invalid format, or a regression with clear causal evidence; otherwise retain inconclusive candidates unchanged. **Retain K0, K1 and K2 unchanged.** Their capability text was injected, has the supplied structured capability format, and the record establishes no leakage. K0’s observed official failure is real but is not a clearly library-caused regression; B0’s success in a single stochastic comparison does not supply that causal link. K1 and recovered K2 passed the official cases, without proving transfer. No retrospective Test selection or tuning is proposed: Test libraries were frozen beforehand, and no Test outcomes are supplied here.

**Confirmed findings:** B0 and K1 passed the complete official evaluation; K0 missed one documented feature interaction while retaining all measured P2P; K2 passed the complete same-patch diagnostic after an incomplete original report. All completed and committed, and local full-suite timing failures were not clean full passes.

**Unresolved hypotheses:** Whether any library altered behavior, efficiency or correctness; why K2’s original report was missing; and why the local performance thresholds failed.

**Specific limitations:** One attempt per cell, partially truncated observations, differing library contents and lengths, no source ablation, no measured performance baseline, and finite verifier coverage. These results are neither statistically significant comparisons nor proof of long-term capability.
